headline: Leafs’ Rielly out day-to-day; Sissons out week-to-week
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Toronto defenseman Morgan Rielly is out day-to-day with a lower-body injury after missing one game, while Colin Sissons was hurt on Sunday night and is out week-to-week.

The Leafs can't afford more losses from the lineup. They sit at 8-9-2 with 18 points through 19 games, and our numbers say the record is not a fluke. TOR has earned 47.1% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality), and that slips to 46% at five-on-five. They are outplaying no one so far this season. What has kept them afloat is finishing: they have scored 6.5 goals more than expected, and their goalies have saved 1.6 more than expected. Both can fade. The special teams are modest too, with the power play creating 0.68 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allowing 0.8. Losing a regular defenseman, even briefly, puts more pressure on a team whose underlying play is already below even and whose results have leaned on above-average finishing.
